title: Timberbound - A fun little Woodcutting Incremental
author: tobias_mueller
selftext:
Hey guys!

After my first post didn't garner much attention, I thought I'd try again after implementing some big changes. (This time I refrained from using AI to help me formulate this post.)

Currently, I am still using Claude Opus 5 to implement my ideas.

One change had by far the biggest impact on the overall feeling and atmosphere of the game: Denser forests and bigger trees. Other than that, I worked on adding subtle mist, updated some tree designs, made the terrain a little more dynamic and increased the tree respawning time by a lot.

The game takes about 50 minutes to 100% and I think that it's quite entertaining for what it is. I know that some skill upgrades near the endgame feel a little useless, as the player is overpowered either way, but I don't mind enough to change that. If some of you scream for a rebalancing, I'll do it though.

Here's a little before/after comparison to give you a feeling of what actually changed:

[Timberbound denser forests before\/after comparison](https://preview.redd.it/3vudm846fdkh1.png?width=3199&format=png&auto=webp&s=083d34b9a7a6c465d6ded4ac95ba53a23ffdb009)

And here's the link to the game: [https://www.gptgames.dev/games/timberbound.html](https://www.gptgames.dev/games/timberbound.html)



I would love to hear some feedback and am happy to answer any questions that arise!

  
One last thing... The game is open source (like the entirety of gptgames) and anyone interested in the development progress can have a look at the earlier versions: [https://github.com/TobiasMue91/tobiasmue91.github.io/commits/main/games/timberbound.html](https://github.com/TobiasMue91/tobiasmue91.github.io/commits/main/games/timberbound.html)  
(Sorry for the lazy commit messages though.)
